title: 宇宙推進工学
subtitle: Space Propulsion
educationalGoal:
Learn how thermal energy systems, mainly liquid rocket engines, are formed and utilized in the aerospace industry, in relation to energy and environmental issues.
In addition, students will learn the basics of rocket and rocket engines and deepen understanding of dreamy space technology.
advice:
Space projects such as the launch of artificial satellites, space travel business by the private sector, and exploration of the moon, Mars, and the solar system by each country government are increasing year by year, and the Age of Discovery of space is expected to arrive in the near future. In space transportation it is necessary to carry the spacecraft including heavy fuel and oxidizer to distant space against gravity. Therefore, in order to expand space development fast, it is essential to develop the ultimate effective use of thermal energy, to significantly reduce transportation costs.
Against this background, in this course, a liquid rocket engine is mainly described as an example to learn how thermal energy systems are useful in aviation and space, and what principles, structures, and design ideas are used to form them. This course is roughly divided into the following contents.
1. General remarks on space engineering
2. Rocket fundamentals
3. Liquid rocket engine design and performance
4. Overview of solid / hybrid rocket, electric propulsion, and ramjet
5. Summary, future technology trends of aerospace engines
By systematically studying the above, students will deepen understanding of dreamy space technology.
books:
Textbooks：Yoshiro Nakamura and Koichi Suzuki, “Rocket Engine”, Morikita shuppan
Reference books：Koichi Suzuki, “Introduction to Space Engineering”, Morikita shuppan
                 George P. Sutton, “Rocket propulsion elements 9th edition”, Wiley
requiredKnowledge:
"thermodynamics I" in the undergraduate course program.
Computational ability based on high school level knowledge of calculus and physics is essential.

activityGoals.body: Understand the rocket fundamentals, staging, and how to obtain the final speed.
Understand the utilization of liquid / electric propulsion.
Understand the effects of nozzle and atmosphere on the performance of rocket engines.
Understand the outline of the basic design of a liquid rocket engine.

achievementLevels.ideal:
(1) Be able to properly explain the basic principle of the rocket, the final arrival speed, and the outline of the flight plan.
(2) Be able to properly explain the design of the liquid rocket engine, the nozzle shape, and the performance impact of the external environment.
(3) Be able to properly explain the characteristics and utilization of various rockets such as electric propulsion and hybrid rockets.
(4) Be able to calculate electric propulsion performance and explain the difference from the chemical rocket performance and the reason appropriately.
achievementLevels.standard:
(1) Be able to explain the basic principle of the rocket, the final arrival speed, and the outline of the flight plan.
(2) Be able to explain the design of the liquid rocket engine, the nozzle shape, and the performance impact of the external environment.
(3) Be able to explain the characteristics and utilization of various rockets such as electric propulsion and hybrid rockets.
(4) Be able to calculate electric propulsion performance and explain the difference from the chemical rocket performance and the reason.
